did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezekiel describes Israel as a “rebellious house”—a people with eyes and ears who refuse to see and hear the word of the LORD.

Did you know? Ezekiel is instructed to prepare “baggage for exile” and demonstrate before the people what it looks like to move from one place to another, so that perhaps they will understand the meaning of the exile that awaits them.
Did you know? One of Ezekiel’s symbolic actions was to dig through a wall in full view of the people and take his belongings out through it, like someone leaving secretly and in distress.
Did you know? Ezekiel is required to carry his belongings on his shoulder in the dark and cover his face; the LORD identifies him as a “sign” to the house of Israel.
Did you know? The LORD explains that Ezekiel’s actions are a symbol of what will happen to the people: the Israelites will go into exile and captivity.
Did you know? The prophet portrays the ruler as someone who will escape secretly but be caught in a snare and brought to Babylon; it is said that he will not see the land to which he is taken.
Did you know? The ruler will not be the only one affected: the people around him and his attendants will also be scattered in every direction, and the sword will pursue them.
Did you know? Ezekiel is instructed to eat his bread trembling and drink his water anxiously, demonstrating the fear that will prevail in Jerusalem and throughout the land of Israel.
Did you know? The people used the proverb, “The days grow long, and every vision comes to nothing,” meaning that the prophecies were being delayed and were not coming true.
Did you know? In response to the claim that the prophecy concerns a distant future, the LORD declares that his word will be spoken and fulfilled, and that it will not be long before it comes to pass.
